newsitem.title: USA: Poster spurs Connecticut deadbeat dad to surrender.
newsitem.headline: Poster spurs Connecticut deadbeat dad to surrender.

text.p: A man who owed $25,000 in back child support payments surrendered to police on Tuesday, a day after seeing his face on a "Wanted" poster, authorities said.
Wayne Barclay, 43, was one of six fathers featured on Connecticut's latest "deadbeat parents" poster, which went on display in post offices and supermarkets across the state Monday.
They owed a total of $300,000 in support payments.
Barclay, who owed $24,605 in support for an 11-year-old daughter, surrendered to Hartford sheriffs Tuesday morning.
"I think it's wonderful," his former wife Linda Barclay said in a statement. "I hope that he will at least resume the responsibility of being a father to his child."

Connecticut's poster campaign, which is also transmitted over the Internet, has been effective in nabbing delinquent parents since it started in 1995, Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said. He said 12 of the 16 fathers named on the previous three posters were arrested.
"The remarkably rapid results of this fourth poster should inspire many others to do the right thing -- show up and pay up, because your day in court is only a matter of time," Blumenthal said.
There are about 140,000 children in Connecticut affected by the problem. In 94 percent of the cases, the parent behind on the court-ordered payments is the father, Blumenthal said.
